seed: Objects of type `marker` under action ACTION6 with touching neighbours [hazard,wall] show mixed outcomes: no_change x2, gone x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Blocks (colour 10 4x4) move together: A1 up, A2 down, A3 apart, A4 together, 4 cells; move iff dest 4x4 all floor 5 (own cells excepted, rows 1-62).
Click by frame colour at the click cell: 9 = arm/switch (blocks->1, clicked marker->11, old active->9); 1 = disarm; 11/other = no-op. That settles the hypothesis: no_change = click on the active marker/non-marker, 'gone' = extractor renaming.
Armed mode: A1-A4 move the active marker's 4x4 cell (marker xy-1) under the same floor rule; A5 no-op but ticks.
HUD: zeros in row 0 from the right and row 63 from the left, width 3(n+1)//7, n = actions since level start; n carried only on exact frame continuity, fallback from bar width.
Unconfirmed: whether clicking an active marker ever does something; level-reset frames handled only via no-bar fallback n=0.
